page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-96-lssd is a high-density compute and storage instance featuring 96 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor with an x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 48 physical cores with hyper-threading, operating at a base speed of 2.3 GHz. It is equipped with 360 GB of RAM, providing 3.75 GB of memory per core. For local storage, the instance bundles 16 local NVMe SSDs totaling 6167 GB of capacity. The processor incorporates advanced instruction sets, including Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix multiplication and vector operations.

Benchmark results indicate exceptional multi-core and memory performance. The instance achieved a Passmark CPU score of 110,513.48 and a multi-core stress-ng CPU performance score of 104,170.8, both placing in the top tiers. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 7,717.61 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 356.38 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. In database and key-value operations, the server demonstrated top-tier capabilities, executing 171.76 million Redis SET operations per second and scoring 34,166.1 on Passmark database operations. Single-core performance is moderate to strong, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2,298.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 2,299.89.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c4-standard-96-lssd offers high resource density by combining massive compute capacity with a large, high-speed local NVMe storage array. This eliminates the need for external storage attachments for IOPS-heavy workloads, though the lack of a bundled GPU limits its efficiency for heavy deep learning training. It is highly suited for data-intensive workloads, including high-throughput database operations, software compilation, static web serving, and medium-scale LLM inference, where it processes 7B model prompts at 319.13 tokens per second.

Operating at 2.3 GHz, the processor supports advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and AMX. Qualitatively, this server offers high resource density by combining massive compute power with fast local storage, making it highly efficient for database hosting, software compilation, and medium-scale LLM inference. However, the absence of a dedicated GPU represents a tradeoff for deep learning workloads.
